title: Open a scored ampoule while retaining its cap inside a protective opener
instruction: Open the inert scored ampoule using the captive opener. Keep the ampoule body upright. Keep both grippers off the cap and neck. Leave the open body in its holder and the cap retained inside the opener on its rack. Release both hands.
context: Ampoule opening is a laboratory and clinical preparation step where a protective opener provides leverage and retains the separated glass cap. This inert replica isolates coordinated breakaway and cap retention. It makes no claim about sterility or medication handling or injury rates.
setup: Official bimanual YAM station. Table top z 0.7475 m. x away from robots and y toward the left arm. Ampoule body is an original rigid 12 mm diameter by 40 mm long inert replica with a 6 mm diameter neck. Body mass 8 g. Its root is at x 260 mm and y 20 mm and z 24 mm above the tabletop. Its bottom rests on a 4 mm high holder floor. Cap is 20 mm long with a maximum diameter of 9 mm and mass 1 g. Cap root is at the neck plane z 44 mm above table. A native fixed neck joint has nominal break torque 0.020 N m and axial break force 20 N. These are prototype parameters pending physical calibration. The plastic opener has a 24 mm square exterior by 83 mm height and total mass 20 g. Its mouth faces downward. Its root starts at x 280 mm and y negative 140 mm and z 84 mm above table. Four passive retaining jaws move radially up to 3 mm. Each jaw mass is 1 g and its spring is 5000 N per metre with damping 5 N seconds per metre and a 5 N force limit. The light blue ampoule geometry represents an inert glass or rigid polymer replica. The blue tool represents rigid plastic with compliant ring behavior approximated by passive jaws. The fixed body holder has a 13 mm opening and 20 mm outer width and an 8 mm wall height on its 4 mm floor. The fixed opener rack has a 70 mm square base and two 44 mm support ledges that hold the downward mouth clear. All authored solids and joint anchors are listed in scene_inventory.json. No medication or patient or real sharp fragment is used.
scoring: 0.25 when the opener covers the cap before a confirmed joint break. A measured neck gap alone can only earn 0.25 while the cap remains covered. Higher scores require a confirmed native joint break. 0.5 when cap base separation from the body neck is at least 12 mm and the entire cap remains inside the tool cavity but the body or tool is not yet returned. 0.75 for the opened body upright within 5 degrees and within 2 mm of the holder target and the opener within 3 mm and 5 degrees of its rack target before both hands are released. 0.9 once both hands are open beyond 35 mm travel and clear of all movable objects and every physical vertex of the body and cap and opener housing and all four jaws stays within a 0.50 mm peak excursion bound and every rigid body orientation changes by at most 1 degree over a continuous one second of native substeps. Any excursion or loss of hand clearance or return pose restarts the complete interval. 1.0 after these release conditions hold for one further continuous second. Permanent zero after direct robot contact within 6 mm of the neck or any direct cap contact within 0.20 mm native contact separation. Permanent zero after any body tilt above 15 degrees or any cap escape once the joint breaks or the neck gap exceeds 0.50 mm or any drop below the tabletop by more than 2 mm or any invalid measurement. Cap base must be laterally within 1.5 mm of the tool axis and from 33 to 41 mm below the tool root. All cap mesh vertices must lie within the 12 mm square protective cavity and between 39 mm below and 40 mm above its root. A video and ruler and angle gauge can score the replica. Force sensor readings are not scoring criteria. All other outcomes score zero.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds.
reset_notes: One epoch per process. A neck is consumed and must be replaced in a physical inert replica. In simulation start a fresh process so that the native breakaway joint is restored before physics initialization. Restore the cap and body poses and all four jaw positions. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Four spring loaded jaws retain a rigid cap after a native joint breaks. The 0.020 N m break torque is a nominal setting for an inert training replica. Matching a physical connector requires calibration. The model omits liquid and glass fragments. It measures tool use and cap retention.
scores: Dream 1 scored 0.0 in 2400 steps. The scripted demonstration scored 1.0 in 502 steps.
